newsitem.title: USA: Conn. picks pool of underwriters, sets bond sales.
newsitem.headline: Conn. picks pool of underwriters, sets bond sales.

text.p: Connecticut, on Friday, selected a new pool of 35 underwriters, creating a special bracket for regional firms, and scheduled a series of debt sales, treasury officials said on Friday.

Paul Silvestor, state treasurer, said the regional firms were chosen for their strong presence in the state. The underwriters in this group were Fleet Securities, Greenwich Partners, Roosevelt & Cross, and Smith Whiley Securities.
Silvester, the former deputy state treasurer, recently replaced Christopher Burnham, who left the post for a private company.
The new treasurer, in prepared remarks, confirmed plans for a sale during the August 11 week of $260 million of general obligation bonds through PaineWebber.
A source in the financial industry earlier provided these details.
Bear, Stearns & Co, Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, Roosevelt & Cross, and Smith Barney will serve as co-senior managers, along with 13 co-managers.

Pat O'Neil, a spokesman, added the state also plans to sell through negotiation in September about $110 million of clean water bonds and in October around $150 million of special transportation bonds. "No one's been chosen to run the books," he said, referring to both bond sales.

For the new, senior manager pool, the state selected Artemis Capital Group, Bear, Stearns & Co, Goldman, Sachs & Co., Merrill Lynch & Co, J.P. Morgan Securities, Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, PaineWebber, Prudential Securities, and Smith Barney, Silvester said.

The co-senior manager pool was composed of Banc One Capital Corp, Bank Boston, M.R. Beal & Co, Belle Haven Investments, BT Securities, Fahnestock & Co., First Southwest, First Union Capital Markets, Gates Capital, Janney Montgomery Scott, WR Lazard Laidlaw, Oppenheimer & Co, Pryor McClendon Counts & Co, Raymond James & Associates, Sibert Bradford Shank & Co, William E. Simon & Sons Municipal Securities, Herbert J. Sims & Co, and Tucker Anthony Inc.
The senior managers for the UCONN program were Advest, A.G. Edwards & Sons, First Albany Corp, and Lehman Bros.
